title: RADICAL Brachioradial Exercises (DON'T NEGLECT THIS MUSCLE!)
summary: A practical tutorial of forearm and brachioradialis exercises NH adapted from arm wrestling training for hypertrophy: preacher hammer curls with a rope or towel, fat-grip cupping preacher curls, dynamic lean-forward preacher curls, rope hangman curls, belt pronation twists, towel pull-ups and cupped fat-grip pull-ups. He stresses a stacked wrist, short ranges of motion and specific rep ranges for each.
claims: He picked arm wrestling training methods for forearm hypertrophy, not to make anyone a better arm wrestler
Beyond dumbbells, forearm training is best done with a rope and a towel
Use the preacher station to lock the elbow and shoulder so the forearm is recruited
On preacher hammer curls with rope or towel, grab a few inches from the plate and lower only until the forearm is parallel to the floor; going deeper rotates the shoulder inward
Always keep the wrist stacked; if the wrist breaks, the set has failed, since an unstacked wrist means tendinitis and poor forearm recruitment
Do rope or towel preacher hammer curls for 6-10 reps because the wrist gives out fast and becomes the limiting factor
Fat-grip preacher curls with a cupping grip (all fingers on one side, no thumb wrap) build the inner forearm and biceps; exaggerate wrist rotation on the way down to keep the weight from rolling out
Use a wide 6-12 rep range on these because reps drop quickly from set to set (e.g. 12, then 9-10)
On the dynamic dumbbell preacher curl, lean the torso forward with the weight while keeping the shoulder joint fixed, and let the weight roll to the knuckles at the bottom to finish with a wrist curl
Only break the stacked wrist when it gives a benefit such as more range of motion and activation
On the hangman curl keep shoulders back and frozen, wrist stacked, no supination, and a limited range; grind sticking points
Hangman curls are safe to push hard because the biceps is not supinated, so there is no tear risk; a cable gives more constant tension than a plate
The brachioradialis is underdeveloped in most people because everyone does supinated curls and rarely neutral-grip ones
Pronation twist: loop a belt or band deep in the hand near the wrist with a plate attached and rotate inward; vary elbow position and angle
Do pronation twists for 10-20 reps rather than heavy like arm wrestlers, since the goal is hypertrophy
For forearm-biased towel pull-ups use a close neutral grip, twist wrists inward on the way up, explode up and lower slowly; half reps at the top bias forearms, full reps add back
Fingers opening on towel pull-ups means undertrained fingers and is partly mental; squeeze like your life depends on it
Cupped fat-grip neutral pull-ups, with hands on top rather than wrapped, are his favourite pull-up for forearms and back; for advanced lifters with strong wrists
Weight the cupped fat-grip pull-ups; 4-6 or 4-8 reps may even be good for hypertrophy
He has small wrists relative to his forearms, yet the forearms grew by training them with arm wrestlers' methods
exercises: grab mid-rope a few inches from plate, forearm to parallel, stacked wrist
cup the fat grip with all fingers on one side, rotate wrist inward on descent
lean torso forward with weight, roll weight to knuckles, finish with wrist curl
more ROM and forearm activation; 6-12 reps
rope through plate or cable, shoulders frozen, no supination, short range
belt deep in hand near wrist, plate hanging, rotate inward
close neutral grip, twist wrists inward going up, partials for forearm bias
hands on top of fat grips, forearms flexed, chest to bar
forearms plus unique lat feel; 6-10 or 4-8 reps
